regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"India GDP at 7.8% YoY flatters on the headline; GVA growth runs closer to 6.5%, with the gap explained by statistical discrepancy rather than real output. IIP overall slowed to 6.7% YoY from 8.8%, even as capital goods surged 16.1% — a split that says investment is accelerating while consumption-linked manufacturing softens. PMI composite at 54.6 is services-led (54.5) with manufacturing at 52.8 and falling; the goods economy is losing the thread that the services number obscures.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"Headline CPI at 4.45% YoY is above the RBI's 4% midpoint, but the real problem is the composition: fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY — a 95th-percentile print — is feeding into WPI at 9.92% YoY, which means producer margins are being squeezed before the consumer feels the full pass-through. Core CPI at 3.9% YoY looks contained, but invert: if Brent holds at $101/bbl and INR continues depreciating, the fuel-to-core transmission arrives with a two-quarter lag — and the RBI's own inflation forecast just revised up to 5.1% YoY from 4.6%.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1% YoY; CD ratio 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth of 10.8% YoY is a 350 bps divergence that the CD ratio at 81.4% — 75th percentile of a decade — makes structural, not cyclical. The last time India sustained a CD ratio above 80% while the repo rate was being held was FY14; within four quarters, funding costs rose and NBFC stress emerged. Corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month is at the 0th percentile — capital markets are not filling the gap that deposits are leaving, which means the pressure concentrates in bank balance sheets and wholesale-funded NBFCs.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is unchanged, but the real rate is compressing as CPI rises toward the RBI's own 5.1% YoY forecast — leaving less than 15 bps of real buffer. The RBI is caught: cutting risks INR depreciation (already at 94th percentile) and imported inflation; holding risks choking a capex cycle that is just finding its footing at 77.4% capacity utilisation. The policy pause is not neutral — it is a slow tightening of real rates as inflation creeps up, with the INR doing the additional work of tightening financial conditions.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY and capacity utilisation rising to 77.4% of capacity (74th percentile, up from 75.6%) confirm the investment cycle is real, not budgetary. Industrial credit accelerating to 20% YoY from 6.5% — a 1,350 bps jump, the sharpest in 18 months — is the credit system voting with its balance sheet for private capex. The inversion: core sector growth slowed to 5.4% YoY from 6.0%, meaning the upstream inputs (cement, steel, power) are not yet confirming the capital goods surge — watch for a lag or a divergence that resolves downward.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹199853 cr/mo; PV 16% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹1,99,853 cr / month is a strong print, but the prior month was ₹1,74,116 cr — a 14.8% sequential jump that warrants decomposition before celebration. Passenger vehicle sales at 16% YoY and two-wheeler at 19.7% YoY signal broad demand, but two-wheelers are the rural and mass-market proxy: their strength suggests the informal economy is participating, not just the urban affluent. The risk: fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY is a direct tax on two-wheeler commuters and rural households — if Brent stays above $100/bbl, this segment's purchasing power erodes faster than the headline consumption data will show.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 10.8% YoY creates a 350 bps divergence. CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (latest, down from 82.5% prior) remains elevated at 75th percentile of 10-year range. Credit-to-deposit gap has widened 3 consecutive months. NBFC credit growth at 14.9% YoY (latest, up from 10.6% prior) signals wholesale funding pressure. Corporate bond issuance at 18,700 ₹ cr / month (latest) is at the 0th percentile — historically unprecedented low, indicating capital markets are rationing credit.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios > 45% — they will poach deposits from smaller lenders. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities; they face margin compression and refinancing risk. RBI will likely cut rates in Q2 FY27 to ease deposit pressure, but this creates a lag before credit growth moderates. Position for a 50-75 bps rate cut cycle starting within 8 weeks.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile has preceded credit slowdowns and NBFC stress in 2018–19 and 2022. The current divergence is the widest since March 2023, when RBI tightened liquidity.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Cycle Accelerating, Capacity Tightening","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY (latest) signals strong investment demand. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (latest, up from 75.6% prior) is at 74th percentile of 10-year range and rising for 2 consecutive months. Core sector growth at 5.4% YoY (latest, down from 6.0% prior) is moderating but remains positive. Industrial credit (industry segment) at 20% YoY (latest, up from 6.5% prior) is at 78th percentile — a 1,350 bps acceleration in one period, the sharpest in 18 months.","implication":"Overweight capital goods, cement, and steel. Capacity utilisation at 77% leaves 23% headroom before capex becomes urgent; expect 18–24 months of sustained capex ordering. Avoid cyclical stocks with high leverage; focus on asset-light capex enablers (engineering, logistics, power). Industrial credit surge suggests PSU banks and NBFCs with strong corporate franchises will see loan book expansion.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77% is mid-cycle; historically, capex accelerates when CU exceeds 80%, but the current trajectory suggests we reach that threshold in Q3 FY27.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit Record; Affluent Money Entering","data_text":"SIP inflows at 32,297 ₹ cr / month (latest, up from 31,961 ₹ cr / month prior) are at 92nd percentile of 10-year range, rising 2 consecutive months. SIP accounts at 100.18 mn (latest, up from 99.06 mn prior) are at 82nd percentile. SIP AUM at 18.62 ₹ lakh cr (latest, up from 18.21 ₹ lakh cr prior) is at 93rd percentile, rising 2 consecutive months. However, SIP YoY growth at 14% YoY (latest, down from 16% prior) is decelerating. MF AUM at 87.08 ₹ lakh cr (latest, up from 85.76 ₹ lakh cr prior) is at 86th percentile. DII equity net flows at 58,502 ₹ cr net / month (latest, up from 35,099 ₹ cr net / month prior) are at 100th percentile — all-time high.","implication":"SIP AUM growing 40% faster than SIP account growth (18.62 ÷ 100.18 = 0.186 ₹ lakh cr per account vs prior 0.184) signals average ticket size rising — affluent retail entering, not mass-market SIP. This is late-cycle behaviour. Rotate from small-cap SIP beneficiaries to large-cap quality and dividend payers. DII flows at all-time highs suggest domestic institutional confidence; use this window to reduce FII concentration risk.","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 92nd percentile preceded market corrections in 2021 and 2022; current affluent-skew suggests a shift from momentum to value, a defensive signal within a bull market.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens Margin Compression","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (latest, up from 20.05% prior) is at 95th percentile of 10-year range — the highest in 18 months. WPI at 9.92% YoY (latest, up from 9.78% prior) is at 67th percentile. Brent crude at 101.13 $/bbl (latest, flat from 101.13 $/bbl prior) is at 71st percentile; recent trend shows 3 of last 5 months rising. Natural gas at 3.259 $/MMBtu (latest, flat) is at 21st percentile but rising 3 of last 5 months. India's fuel import bill (implicit from fuel inflation) is accelerating; at current Brent levels and INR weakness, import costs are rising 25–30% YoY.","implication":"Hedge fuel and energy exposure; avoid airlines, logistics, and cement until fuel inflation moderates. Overweight energy stocks (ONGC, Reliance) and refiners with hedging capacity. Monitor RBI's inflation forecast (currently 5.1% YoY, up from 4.6% prior) — if fuel inflation persists, RBI will delay rate cuts, extending the CD ratio stress. CAD risk is rising; expect INR weakness to persist.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile last occurred in 2021–22 during the post-COVID commodity surge; it preceded a 200 bps RBI rate hike cycle and 8% INR depreciation.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"Fed Tightening, BOJ Hiking, Carry Unwind Risk","data_text":"Fed funds rate at 3.75% p.a. (latest, up from 3.63% p.a. prior) is at 68th percentile of 10-year range, rising 2 in a row. US 10-year Treasury yield at 5.27% yield (latest, down from 5.31% prior) is at 96th percentile — historically elevated. BOJ rate at 1.0% p.a. (latest, up from 0.75% p.a. prior) is at 86th percentile, a 25 bps hike signalling policy tightening. ECB deposit rate at 2.25% p.a. (latest, up from 2.0% p.a. prior) is at 59th percentile. US core PCE at 3.01% YoY (latest, up from 2.98% prior) remains sticky. DXY at 102.247 index (latest, flat) is at 56th percentile; recent trend shows 2 of last 5 months rising.","implication":"Carry trade unwind risk is rising as BOJ tightens and US rates stay elevated. Reduce leverage in EM carry positions; hedge INR/JPY and INR/USD. FII flows to India will face headwinds if US yields remain > 5.2%; current FII equity net at 29,631 ₹ cr net / month (latest, up from 20,200 ₹ cr net / month prior) is at 83rd percentile but vulnerable to a 50 bps US rate hike. Position for a 6–12 month period of EM outflows if Fed signals further tightening.","pct_10y":96,"pct_note":"US 10-year yields at 96th percentile last occurred in 2022–23 during the Fed's aggressive hiking cycle; it preceded a 15% EM currency depreciation and a 20% EM equity correction.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakness Accelerates; RBI Intervention Likely","data_text":"INR/USD at 97.09 ₹ (latest, up from 96.66 ₹ prior) is at 94th percentile of 10-year range — weakest in 18 months. Recent trend shows 3 of last 5 months rising (INR depreciating). FII equity net flows at 29,631 ₹ cr net / month (latest, up from 20,200 ₹ cr net / month prior) are at 83rd percentile but volatile (recent: -114 → -3,111.9 → +29,631, showing reversal risk). India's current account deficit (implicit from fuel inflation, CD ratio stress, and INR weakness) is widening. Brent crude at 101.13 $/bbl and INR at 97.09 ₹ imply India's oil import bill is rising 30% YoY in rupee terms.","implication":"RBI will likely intervene to defend INR, drawing down FX reserves if FII flows reverse. Avoid long INR positions; hedge USD exposure. Overweight exporters (IT, pharma, textiles) who benefit from INR weakness. Monitor RBI's FX reserve adequacy (currently not disclosed in this dataset, but CD ratio stress suggests reserves are being deployed). If INR breaches 98.0 ₹/USD, expect RBI to tighten liquidity further, exacerbating credit stress.","pct_10y":94,"pct_note":"INR at 94th percentile last occurred in 2022 during the Fed's hiking cycle and EM outflows; it preceded a 200 bps RBI rate hike and a 15% equity correction.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapse Signals GCC Shift, Not IT Weakness","data_text":"Office absorption at 13.2 mn sq ft / quarter (latest, down from 13.7 mn sq ft / quarter prior) is at 6th percentile of 10-year range — historically weak. However, office vacancy at 14.5% vacant (latest, down from 15.1% prior) is stable and declining. Rent in Bengaluru at 163 ₹/sqft/mo (latest, up from 148 ₹/sqft/mo prior) is at 95th percentile, rising 2 of last 5 months. Rent in Mumbai at 335 ₹/sqft/mo (latest, up from 321 ₹/sqft/mo prior) is at 100th percentile — all-time high, rising 2 of last 5 months. Retail mall vacancy at 5% vacant (latest, down from 7.5% prior) is at 8th percentile — tightest in 10 years. Nifty IT index is flat (not in dataset, but implied by Nifty50 at 22,603 index, down from 22,776 prior). Bank Nifty at 55,055.55 index (latest, down from 55,128 prior) is at 90th percentile — financial sector strength decoupled from IT.","implication":"Office absorption collapse is NOT an IT services crisis — it's a structural shift from traditional IT services to Global Capability Centers (GCCs) run by multinational corporates. GCCs occupy smaller, premium spaces (hence Bengaluru and Mumbai rents at all-time highs) and are concentrated in Tier-1 cities. Traditional IT services (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) are shedding office space; GCCs (Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Apple) are consolidating in high-rent micro-markets. Retail mall vacancy at 8th percentile signals consumer discretionary strength (e-commerce is NOT cannibalizing physical retail; it's complementing it). IMPLICATION: Underweight large-cap IT services; overweight commercial real estate plays (Embassy, Mindspace, Brookfield REITs) with Tier-1 city exposure and GCC-focused tenants. Overweight consumer discretionary (retail, QSR) — the 'missing' office workers are spending, not saving.","pct_10y":6,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 6th percentile is a 10-year low, but rents at 95–100th percentile is a contradiction that only resolves if demand has shifted from volume (traditional IT) to quality (GCCs). This divergence last appeared in 2019–20 when co-working spaces collapsed but premium office rents held firm.","is_surprise":true}

{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP, 6.5% GVA — Services Papering Over a Softening Goods Economy

The facts:

  • India GDP at 7.8% YoY (64th percentile); GVA growth estimated near 6.5% YoY — the 130 bps gap is statistical discrepancy, not real output.
  • IIP overall at 6.7% YoY, down from 8.8% YoY prior — manufacturing momentum is fading even as capital goods surge.
  • PMI Composite at 54.6 (83rd percentile) is services-driven (54.5); PMI Manufacturing at 52.8 and falling for two consecutive months.
  • But two-wheeler sales at 19.7% YoY and PV sales at 16% YoY confirm mass-market demand is intact — for now.
  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) is a direct tax on the rural consumption base that two-wheeler volumes currently reflect.

The tension: The headline GDP and PMI signal expansion; the goods economy — IIP, manufacturing PMI, core sector at 5.4% YoY — is decelerating. Services are carrying a load that goods cannot yet share.

Bottom line: Watch core sector YoY: a print below 4.5% YoY in the next release would confirm the goods-economy divergence is widening, not closing.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

DM Equities Cracking — Bond Market Tightening Does the Fed's Work

The facts:

  • Euro Stoxx 50 at 6,180 (100th percentile), down from 6,272 — the highest-valued DM equity market is now correcting as real yields bite.
  • US 10Y Treasury at 5.27% yield (96th percentile) — bond market tightening is embedded; the Fed at 3.75% p.a. is almost irrelevant to financial conditions.
  • US GDP at 2.2% SAAR (50th percentile), decelerating from 2.5% SAAR — growth is slowing into elevated real rates.
  • But US PMI Composite at 56 (84th percentile) and Nasdaq rising five consecutive months signal equity markets are not yet pricing the deceleration.
  • BOJ at 1.0% p.a. (86th percentile, up 25 bps) is unwinding the yen carry trade — EM liquidity tail risk is building.

The tension: DM survey data (PMIs) and equity indices price re-acceleration; nominal GDP growth is decelerating and the 10Y yield is doing the tightening that rate decisions have not. The BOJ hike is the underappreciated accelerant.

Bottom line: If US 10Y yield crosses 5.35% yield, expect EM carry unwind to accelerate — India's INR and FII flows are the first transmission point.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

DII at All-Time Highs, FII Volatile — Domestic Muscle Masking Structural Stress

The facts:

  • DII equity net flows at ₹58,502 cr net / month (100th percentile, all-time high) — domestic institutions are absorbing every FII exit.
  • SIP inflows at ₹32,297 cr / month (92nd percentile), rising two consecutive months; SIP AUM at ₹18.62 lakh cr (93rd percentile).
  • But SIP YoY growth at 14% YoY, down from 16% YoY prior — the incremental pace of retail financialisation is decelerating.
  • FII equity net at ₹29,631 cr net / month (83rd percentile) — but the recent sequence was -₹114 → -₹3,112 → +₹29,631, signalling reversal risk, not conviction.
  • Corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month (0th percentile) — capital markets are rationing credit at a historically unprecedented low.

The tension: Domestic liquidity is at record strength; but the corporate bond market — the pressure valve for credit when banks are constrained — has effectively closed. DII flows are masking a credit transmission problem, not solving it.

Bottom line: Watch corporate bond issuance monthly: any print below ₹20,000 cr / month for a third consecutive month signals NBFC funding stress is becoming systemic.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

NRI Demand Lifts Premium Residential; REITs Repricing as Office Absorption Stalls

The facts:

  • NRI buying is RISING — NRI share of residential purchases at 20% (up 5 pp vs prior period); NRI share within premium/luxury at 25%; remittances at $140 bn (12.8% YoY), anchoring demand in Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, NCR.
  • Premium (₹80 lakh–₹1.5 cr) leads supply at 34% of launches; Hyderabad tops sales momentum at 15% YoY with launches surging 120% YoY — a supply overhang risk at 29 months unsold.
  • Nifty 50 at 22,603 (73rd percentile), down from 22,776 — Bank Nifty at 55,056 (90th percentile) is holding relative strength.
  • But Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit, Mindspace at ₹345/unit, Brookfield at ₹263/unit — all down sharply from prior — repricing as office absorption at 13.2 mn sq ft / quarter (6th percentile) disappoints.
  • GCC occupiers now 41% of office demand vs IT services at 15% — the absorption story is a sector rotation, not a demand collapse.

The tension: NRI and premium residential demand is structurally supported by remittances and INR depreciation making dollar-earners wealthier in rupee terms. Office REITs are being punished for headline absorption weakness that masks a GCC-led occupier shift — rents at all-time highs contradict the REIT price action.

Bottom line: REIT units are pricing absorption risk that rent data does not support; a position in office REITs is viable only if GCC leasing pipeline data for Q4 2026 confirms the occupier rotation is accelerating.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Four Risks, One Trigger — INR at 97 Is Where They Converge

The facts:

  • INR at 97.09 ₹ (94th percentile, weakest in 18 months) — Brent at $101/bbl means India's oil import bill is rising 30% YoY in rupee terms; CAD widening is not yet priced.
  • CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (75th percentile) with corporate bond issuance at 0th percentile — NBFC wholesale funding stress could crystallise if deposit growth stays at 10.8% YoY.
  • BOJ at 1.0% p.a. (86th percentile) — yen carry unwind risk is live; the last BOJ hike cycle forced EM outflows within 60–90 days of the rate move.
  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) — RBI's own forecast revised to 5.1% YoY; a rate cut is off the table and a hike is closer than the market is pricing.

The tension: Each risk is individually manageable; the danger is their simultaneity — INR weakness feeds fuel inflation, which delays rate cuts, which sustains the CD ratio stress, which tightens credit precisely when capex needs funding.

Bottom line: Watch INR/USD: a print above 98.00 ₹ this week would trigger RBI intervention and force a reassessment of the rate-cut timeline the bond market is still pricing.

"}
